column1: # Pokémon Pokopia (Koei Tecmo KTGL engine, Switch 2 / NVN2), update 1.0.4 (v327680). Started from the NSP script's provisional profile and brought up on the Mac:
# boots, plays through the opening into the first area at 60 fps. Build: scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py <dump folder> --platform mac-app --gpu none

# Switch 2: games get 9 GB of the 12 GB (as Donkey Kong Bananza's profile). Pokopia's engine allocates a 5.2 GB block at start (main+0x1040240: aligned_alloc 0x135c07008), which the guessed 3.25 GB heap refused, and nnMain returned at once
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region
# the NPDM declares 0 MB of system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon (Big Brain Academy: Brain vs. Brain sets a heap only then)
# used memory for the current rewritten modules, at least the default 64 MB
# KTGL rewrites control section +0x20..+0x27 when it loads a shader (its G2S files hold other values there): masked in the key (shader_split.py key_ctl, hle_nvn.c keys_hash)
# 72 programs are built at run time from code no game file holds as stored (the language menu among them): each build boots the game once with DM_NVN_SHDUMP
# and these DM_KEYS steps (English, the intro, the trainer, the character creator, the first area) to capture them from the user's own copy (build_ipa_from_nsp.py capture_shader_dumps)
# the game's dynamic resolution measures its GPU time with counter timestamps: with one time per submission it saw none and kept 1920x1080, 40-45 fps behind Tangrowth on an M4
# MacBook Air; with the segments' own times it lowers the 3D view (1728x972 there) and holds 60
